title: Favorite drummer and clarinetists
summary: He picks Nene as the best drummer and George Lewis as his favorite clarinetist, and recalls Johnny Dodds, Georgia Boy and Zeb.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Who was the best drummer you can remember working with or hearing in the old days?
I think you heard when you were a kid even if you can remember.

Well, I think I would pick, I'll pick Nene out of all of them. I'll pick Nene way back there. He was a wonderful drummer. Yeah, he was a good drummer. Yeah, for jazz. Very good. Had the right beat. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. You really could swing, you know, with them hitting the drums.
What about clarinet players? Who were the best in those days?

Well, the clarinet player? Well, I think, let's see, well, let's see who I got on clarinet there I used to like so much was, well, I would say George. George is the man I always liked on clarinet. George Lewis. George Lewis. Yeah. I liked the George on.
Do you remember any of the men before him like T.O. or Bach K?
Well, T.O. or Bach K, well I just know of them. Johnny Dodds. Johnny Dodds of him. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. He left a good while ago. I remember about him though.
Do you remember Georgia Boy? Georgia Boy, yeah.
What did he play? Well, that was, he played, Georgia Boy played, what you call him, didn't he? Georgia Boy.

Yeah, that's what I say. He played the clarinet too. Georgia Boy. That was another good one. You made me think of that. Yeah, I remember him, yeah. Yeah, Georgia Boy was very good on clarinet. Do you remember Zeb?
Well, see Zeb. I remember that, I remember that name. I remember that name Zeb though. Yeah.
